chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) that he was asked about a man who dies and has no heir and no agnate, and he said:
He bequeaths his wealth wherever he wishes among Muslims, the poor, and the wayfarer.
As for what the report contained of his saying: 'The man is more entitled to his wealth as long as the soul is in him,' and similarly what contained that, we have cited it in our Great Book.

The ruling regarding it is that he is more entitled to his wealth if he disposes of it during his life and clarifies it from his ownership. As for if he bequeaths it, it is not executed except in the third.

key_terms.عَصَبَة: Agnates (male relatives who inherit by residue)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of a Muslim who dies without any heirs or agnates?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the distinction between lifetime disposal of wealth, which is absolute, and posthumous bequest (wasiyyah), which is restricted to one-third of the estate. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that in the absence of heirs or agnates, the deceased retains full discretion to allocate his assets to the general Muslim community, the poor, or travelers, provided the bequest does not exceed the standard one-third limit. This ruling underscores the principle that ownership persists as long as the soul remains, but testamentary execution is subject to specific legal boundaries.
